title: Intermittent keyed queue reordering
instruction:
Jobs occasionally overtake earlier jobs for the same account, and shutdown sometimes returns before accepted work has finished. Inspect src/, logs/incident.log and the native tests; find and fix the underlying causes and add deterministic regressions. The timer, retry helper and job normalizer are plausible suspects, but do not replace the queue with a single global serial executor or add arbitrary sleeps.

The public createQueue({onEvent}) API returns submit(key,fn), drain(), close(), and stats(). A key is a nonempty string, fn is a function; invalid submissions reject without events or counter changes. Accepted work starts in FIFO submission order per key, with at most one running function for that key; different keys progress independently. A thrown/rejected job rejects only its own submission, never poisons later work. drain() is a fence for ALL jobs accepted before that call (including queued ones); work accepted later must not delay that particular fence. close() stops acceptance immediately, rejects new submissions with code QUEUE_CLOSED, and resolves only once accepted jobs finish; repeated close() calls have the same effect.

stats() returns {accepted,completed,failed,running,pending}, where pending means accepted but not yet started. Event callback receives {type:'start'|'finish',key}; callback failures are ignored, job failures still count as completed and failed. Preserve the existing service/client adapters and genuine per-key parallelism. No external dependencies.
